words.definition: present, or seeming to be present, everywhere at once
words.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.

words.definition: to make a problem or bad situation worse
words.example: Cutting the support programme will only exacerbate the housing crisis.

words.definition: showing great attention to detail; very careful and thorough
words.example: She kept meticulous records of every transaction.

words.definition: a turning point after which things change significantly
words.example: The discovery marked a watershed moment in the treatment of the disease.

words.definition: to admit, often reluctantly, that something is true
words.example: He finally conceded that his original plan had failed.

words.definition: in spite of; without being affected by
words.example: Notwithstanding the delays, the project was finished on budget.

words.definition: to support or form the basis of a theory, idea or system
words.example: These principles underpin the entire legal system.
The plan worked, albeit more slowly than expected.

words.definition: a broadly accurate practical guide, not based on exact calculation
words.example: As a rule of thumb, you should save at least ten per cent of your income.

words.definition: to find a way around a difficulty, rule or obstacle
words.example: The company found a legal way to circumvent the new regulations.

words.definition: very weak or slight; barely strong enough to hold together
words.example: The link between the two events is, at best, tenuous.

words.definition: happening at the same time as, or working together with, something else
words.example: The two departments now work in tandem to avoid duplicating effort.
